overview.title: The tool that didn't exist.
overview.lead: Justice-impacted people face a hiring system that treats their record as an automatic disqualifier. No tool combined AI career analysis, record-aware legal navigation, and disclosure coaching in one place. Until now.
overview.lead2: This page is the complete documentation of what this platform is, how it works, what research grounds it, and how every decision was made. Open source. Nothing hidden. Designed to be read by scholars, funders, developers, and partner organizations.

stats.s1: Employed in year one after release
stats.s3: Tools that combined AI career analysis, legal navigation, and disclosure coaching in one place before this one

overview.journeyLead: Six stages. One platform. Every stage builds on the last. Free at every step.

j0.name: The Forge
j0.what: Upload a resume or describe your work history. Answer a few questions about goals, barriers, readiness, and record. The Forge outputs a resume, a cover letter, career paths matched to your background, and a resource plan. All of it is in plain language.
j0.tech: Claude Sonnet (Anthropic) with a custom prompt scaffold that enforces the 10 behavioral rules. Resume parsed via OCR + NLP. Output hashed and logged.

j1.name: Profile and Job Board
j1.what: Fill in your contact info. Search real listings from several job sources. Employers we checked for hiring people with records are marked, and each mark shows where it applies.
j1.tech: Each mark rests on dated evidence in the employer directory (Neon PostgreSQL) that expires on its own, and it applies only where the evidence was found. No AI summary can grant a mark.

j2.name: Application Tailor
j2.what: Build job-targeted resume versions for specific listings. The AI tailors language to the job description while preserving your story.
j2.tech: Refinery Artifact system: each resume is versioned, stored with metadata (target job, company, application ID), and linked to the job application tracker.

j3.name: Disclosure Planner
j3.what: Plan when and how to talk about your record with specific employers. The planner walks through timing, framing, and what to say. It is grounded in actual Ban-the-Box law and research on employers that hire people with records.
j3.tech: Structured coaching dialogue with t.ROY. Output saved as a disclosure_plan artifact. Nothing in the practice transcript is stored.

j4.name: Interview Practice
j4.what: Text or live voice mock interviews tailored to your target role. Behavioral, situational, and disclosure-specific questions. Real-time feedback on framing, specificity, and narrative arc.
j4.tech: Text mode: Claude Sonnet. Voice mode: OpenAI Whisper (transcription) + Claude (feedback). We never store practice audio. Text practice keeps the feedback, not the conversation. Voice practice keeps a text transcript only when the person turns saving on.

j5.name: Applications + Follow-Up
j5.what: Track every application: company, status, dates, which resume version you used. Generate follow-up emails and save them to the Library.
j5.tech: job_application table in Neon. Refinery Artifact system for follow-up emails and cover letters. Library = everything you made (the My resumes page).

overview.protocolLead: t.ROY follows 10 non-negotiable rules on every interaction. They are hard constraints derived from peer-reviewed research and Troy's decade of direct service. They cannot be overridden by user prompting.

r0.rule: Name the feeling before solving the problem
r0.why: Affect labeling reduces amygdala reactivity before high-stakes work begins (Lieberman et al., 2007).

r1.why: Deficit-first framing activates threat response. Asset-first activates approach motivation.

r2.why: t.ROY is a career guide, not a lawyer. It flags disclosure moments and points to resources.

r3.rule: Match complexity to the user's stated readiness
r3.why: Cognitive load theory: overwhelming someone mid-crisis loses them permanently.

r4.rule: Offer the next step. Never a lecture.
r4.why: Autonomy-supportive language predicts sustained engagement (Deci & Ryan, 2000).

r5.why: The platform is written at a 6th-grade reading level. People in crisis don't need vocabulary tests.

r6.why: People who construct bad-to-good story arcs show measurably better post-release outcomes (McAdams, 2013).

r7.why: Surveillance trauma is real. Trust must be built, not assumed.

r8.why: Unexplained AI advice erodes trust. t.ROY explains its reasoning in plain language every time.

r9.rule: If someone is in crisis, stop and redirect
r9.why: A crisis disclosure during career coaching requires a human, not a chatbot. Full stop.

d0.us: AI career analysis built for justice-impacted people, with employment gaps, records, and barriers included in the model
d0.them: Generic resume builders that treat a 10-year gap as a red flag

d1.us: Record-aware disclosure coaching built into the Refinery as a core tool
d1.them: Job boards that surface Ban-the-Box listings but give no guidance on what to say when asked

d2.us: Most AI steps logged with an input fingerprint, the model, a short note and the time taken, so you can see what ran and when

d3.us: 10 documented, non-negotiable behavioral rules, grounded in research, that govern every t.ROY response
d3.them: A generic chatbot tuned for engagement, not outcomes

d4.us: Consent-gated partner dashboard where organizations see only clients who have explicitly opted in
d4.them: Program tools that harvest participant data without meaningful consent

d5.us: Free at every step. No paywall, no credit card, and no data sold, ever.
d5.them: Freemium tools that paywall the parts people actually need

d6.us: Built by someone who went through the same system firsthand
d6.them: Tools designed by people who have never been incarcerated, for people who have

overview.privacyLead: Surveillance trauma is real. Many justice-impacted people have been monitored, recorded, and reported on without their knowledge or consent for years. This platform is designed to actively undo that pattern.

p0.title: Practice transcripts are saved only by choice
p0.detail: Text interview practice keeps the role, the frame practiced and the coach's feedback, not the conversation. Voice interview practice and disclosure rehearsal keep an encrypted text transcript only when the person turns saving on, and the person can delete it. Audio is never stored by us. Programs cannot read practice through sharing; with progress sharing on, they see a count of sessions.

p1.title: Partner access is consent-gated
p1.detail: Partner organizations (nonprofits, reentry programs, job centers) can only see clients who have explicitly opted in to share their progress. The toggle is in Settings. Off by default. Only the user can turn it on. The partner cannot.

p2.title: Forge data stays local until you choose otherwise
p2.detail: The Forge runs client-side. Resume data, goals, and story answers are stored in your browser's localStorage, not on our servers, until you create an account and choose to sync. You can complete the Forge and never create an account.

p3.title: No data sold, ever
p3.detail: Steel Man Resumes is not funded by advertising. There is no data monetization layer. This is documented in the AGPL-3.0 license and the source code is public.

p4.title: Right to deletion
p4.detail: Settings > Privacy > Delete all data removes everything server-side and clears localStorage. The deletion is immediate and irreversible.

overview.researchLead: Every design decision is grounded in peer-reviewed research. The behavioral protocol, the copy reading level, the narrative arc of the Forge output, and the privacy model all trace to specific empirical literature.

c0.finding: Affect labeling reduces amygdala reactivity by up to 50%
c0.detail: Putting feelings into words activates prefrontal cortex and dampens the stress response. The Forge uses narrative reframing at every step as a documented performance technique that lowers cognitive resistance before high-stakes work. It is not therapy.

c1.finding: Redemption narrative sequences predict higher well-being and post-release stability
c1.detail: People who construct bad-to-good story arcs show measurably better outcomes across health, relationships, and stability. The Forge output is structured as a redemption arc, not a deficit report. That structure replicates a documented psychological mechanism.

c2.finding: Autonomy, competence, and relatedness are the three non-negotiable psychological needs
c2.detail: Incarceration systematically strips all three. This platform rebuilds them: user-driven choices (autonomy), skills surfaced from real history (competence), and language grounded in lived experience rather than clinical distance (relatedness).

c3.finding: Stigma-based discrimination persists even in Ban-the-Box jurisdictions
c3.detail: Removing the checkbox doesn't remove the bias. The Refinery's disclosure coaching prepares users for the form and for the conversation that happens after the application.

c4.finding: Cognitive load undermines decision quality under economic stress
c4.detail: Scarcity (of money, time, housing stability) taxes cognitive bandwidth directly. The platform is designed for people under maximum load: short prompts, no jargon, one question at a time, no decision fatigue.

c5.finding: Workforce reentry programs with wraparound support show 2-3x better employment retention
c5.detail: Employment alone doesn't stick. The Refinery is a wraparound: resume + disclosure + interview + applications + coaching, in one place, free.

overview.archLead: Most AI steps are logged with a keyed, one-way fingerprint of the input (never the input itself), the model, a short note and the time taken. Resume reading, fact checks and voice practice are not in this log, and without an account the note holds none of the words a person typed. Built for funder reporting, compliance review, and program evaluation.

arch.a0: Neon PostgreSQL: all structured data (users, profiles, artifacts, applications, consent records, decision log)
arch.a1: Cloudflare R2: encrypted document storage (uploaded resumes, generated PDFs)
arch.a2: Vercel: serverless hosting, edge functions, preview deployments
arch.a3: Resend: transactional email (magic links only, no marketing email)
arch.a4: Airtable: verified employer data source (manually curated, imported to PostgreSQL)

overview.partnersLead: Reentry programs, workforce development orgs, legal aid societies, and job centers can integrate Steel Man Resumes into their client workflow. Access codes unlock higher AI usage limits and allow consent-gated progress tracking.

n0.label: Access code
n0.detail: One code per program. Clients enter it at sign-in to unlock higher limits. Codes are linked to your partner account.

n1.label: Partner dashboard
n1.detail: See cohort progress (stage, artifacts completed, last activity) for clients who have opted in to share. CSV export for program reporting.

n2.label: No vendor lock-in
n2.detail: AGPL-3.0 license. The source code is public. You can self-host a private instance for your program.

n3.label: To get an access code
n3.detail: Email Steel Man Resumes directly. Free for nonprofits and community organizations during the launch period.

overview.fundersLead: The platform is AGPL-3.0 open source and free to all users. No revenue is generated from user data.

n0.label: Measurable outputs
n0.detail: Every Forge completion, resume built, disclosure plan, interview session, and application tracked, with user consent and without collecting PII in aggregate reports.

n1.label: Audit trail
n1.detail: The decision_log table records most AI steps: which tool ran, which model, a one-way fingerprint of the input, the time taken and tokens used, and a short note for signed-in users. Resume reading and fact checks are not in it. For voice practice it records that a session started, never what is said. Funders can request reports on AI performance, model usage, and outcome signals.

n2.label: Target population
n2.detail: Justice-impacted adults in Wisconsin (initial), Midwest (expansion), national (AGPL self-host). Primary focus: people within 90 days of release or recently released.

n3.label: No paywall, by design
n3.detail: The platform will never charge users. Sustainability comes from organizational licensing, grants, and eventual nonprofit status.

overview.livedTitle: Built by someone who lived it
overview.lived1: Steel Man Resumes was built by Troy Carr, a justice-impacted workforce advocate with a decade of direct service navigating the same system these tools are designed to help people survive.
overview.lived2: The platform reflects what he wished existed when he was in it: one place that understood records, didn't treat gaps as disqualifiers, and gave plain-language guidance instead of generic advice designed for people who have never been incarcerated.
overview.lived3: The research is real. The behavioral rules are real. The employers are verified. The privacy model was designed with surveillance trauma in mind because Troy has lived that too.
